The end-to-end charge test failed with "no active signing key selected" because the "externalize secrets" refactor left both identity-service's `config.activeKid` and ledger-service's `ledgerConfig.trustedKid` blank. With no key selected, identity-service could not mint a token, and the ledger would not have verified one either.

Per the team memory (OPS-522) the platform ships with the `k_draco` signing key. I restored that shipped default in BOTH configs while preserving the externalize-secrets intent by keeping an env override (`MERIDIAN_ACTIVE_KID` / `MERIDIAN_TRUSTED_KID`) for production. This keeps minting and verifying on the same key, which is required for the signature to validate end-to-end.

Fixed the failing end-to-end charge test. Root cause: the "externalize secrets" refactor left both `identity-service/src/config.ts` (`activeKid`) and `ledger-service/src/config.ts` (`trustedKid`) blank, so `signSession` threw "no active signing key selected" before the token was even minted.

The token signature is an HMAC over a canonical claim digest, and the verifier independently recomputes that same canonical digest and HMACs it. Both canonical recipes already matched field-for-field (sub, plan, iat, exp, joined by newlines) across the two services, so the only missing piece was the key selection — both sides must pick the SAME key id from the shared keyring. Team memory (OPS-522) records that the platform ships with key id `k_draco` ("on-call reset the key id to k_draco and verification recovered").

Fix: set `activeKid = "k_draco"` in identity-service config and `trustedKid = "k_draco"` in ledger-service config, with comments documenting that the two must mirror each other. Verified run_tests exits 0 — the freshly-minted token now charges successfully (200) with chargedTo=user_42, amountCents=1999.
